result.topic_en: Euler states and solves Problem II: finding a space curve in coordinates x, y, z that makes the integral of (y+z) dy dz / dx a maximum or minimum, deriving the three Euler equations and integrating them to get x as a function of p.
result.transcription:
26
Problema II.
Invenire lineam curvam ternis coordinatis x, y et z contentam, in qua haec formula integralis: $\int\frac{(y+z)\partial y\partial z}{\partial x}$ maximum minimumve obtineat valorem.
Solutio.
16. Posito hic $\partial y=p\partial x$ et $\partial z=p'\partial x=q\partial x$, erit $V=pq(y+z)$, hincque differentiando:
$\partial V=pq\partial y+pq\partial z+(y+z)q\partial p+(y+z)p\partial q.$
Unde, facta comparatione cum formula generali:
$\partial V=M\partial x+N\partial y+N'\partial z+P\partial p+P'\partial p'$,
habebimus $M=0$; $N=pq$; $N'=pq$; $P=(y+z)q$ et $P'=(y+z)p$; hinc ergo fiet $S=V-Pp-P'q=-pq(y+z)$.
Ex his jam tres nostrae aequationes erunt:
1°. $0=-\partial.pq.(y+z)$;
2°. $pq\partial x=\partial.(y+z)q$;
3°. $pq\partial x=\partial.(y+z)p$.
Prima statim praebet $pq(y+z)=a$, ita ut sit $y+z=\frac{a}{pq}$, qui valor, in reliquis substitutus, dat:
1°. $pq\partial x=\partial.\frac{a}{p}=-\frac{a\partial p}{pp}$; 2°. $pq\partial x=\partial.\frac{a}{q}=-\frac{a\partial q}{qq}$.
Hinc sequitur fore $\frac{\partial p}{pp}=\frac{\partial q}{qq}$; consequenter $-\frac{1}{p}=-\frac{1}{q}+b$, sive $\frac{1}{p}=\frac{1}{q}+b$, unde elicimus $q=\frac{cp}{c+p}$. Sicque prima aequatio fit $y+z=\frac{a(c+p)}{cpp}$; reliquae vero dant $pq\partial x=-\frac{a\partial p}{pp}$, ideoque $\partial x=-\frac{a(c+p)\partial p}{cp^4}$, cujus integrale praebet $x=\frac{a}{3p^3}+\frac{a}{2cpp}+f$.
